name: universal-agent-skills
description: Portable coding-agent skills for consistent implementation and verification workflows, plus audits for security, readiness, accessibility, operations and more.

interface.longDescription: Share a canonical set of Agent Skills across Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, and compatible tools: coding conventions, verification workflows, and reviews for security, production readiness, accessibility, operations, data, APIs, AI features and repositories.
defaultPrompt: Use $coding-style while editing this codebase.
Use $simplify-code to simplify code without changing behavior.
Use $surgical-implementation to keep the change minimal and goal-driven.
Use $verify-changes before reporting completion.
Use $no-ai-traces for commit messages, pull requests, and delivered docs.
Use $docs-consolidation when writing or reorganizing project documentation.
Use $secret-hygiene whenever work could touch credentials.
Use $data-minimization when handling test data, logs, or personal records.
Use $supply-chain-pinning when adding or updating dependencies.
Use $destructive-ops-approval before irreversible operations.
Use $license-compliance before copying or vendoring third-party code.
Use $accessibility-audit to audit against every WCAG 2.2 A and AA criterion.
Use $ai-feature-review to reliability, evaluation, safety, privacy and cost of AI features.
Use $api-design-review to rEST, GraphQL, gRPC, realtime, webhook and SDK surfaces.
Use $architecture-review to structure, risks and technical debt with a prioritized plan.
Use $cli-and-scripts-audit to make CLIs, shell and PowerShell scripts safe and portable.
Use $data-audit to schemas, migrations, queries, integrity, backups and pipelines.
Use $debug to find the root cause and fix it properly.
Use $describe-changes to commit messages and pull request descriptions.
Use $explain-codebase to an onboarding guide to an unfamiliar project.
Use $full-project-audit to score every area of a project and plan the remaining checks.
Use $implement-feature to plan, build, test and verify a feature.
Use $improve-prompt to turn any prompt into a clear, model-agnostic one.
Use $incident-response to stabilize, diagnose, then write a blameless postmortem.
Use $infrastructure-audit to review IaC, containers, Kubernetes, Nix and CI without applying.
Use $legal-compliance-review to privacy, consumer-protection, marketing and licensing risks.
Use $operations-audit to observability, deployments, backups, recovery and resilience.
Use $performance-audit to find and fix the bottlenecks that matter, with measurements.
Use $prepare-release to version, changelog, release notes and verified artifacts.
Use $production-readiness-review to decide whether a project is ready for production.
Use $refactor to make code simpler without changing behavior.
Use $repository-audit to docs, licensing, metadata, history, automation and releases.
Use $review-code to review a diff, branch or pull request.
Use $security-audit to find exploitable vulnerabilities with a 76-item checklist.
Use $start-project to scaffold a project with its whole baseline in place.
Use $threat-model to design-level threats, controls and mitigations.
Use $upgrade-dependencies to upgrade packages and runtimes safely, security fixes first.
Use $ux-review to usability, states, copy, emails, localization and CLI ergonomics.
Use $write-agent-instructions to an accurate AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md for a repository.
Use $write-docs to make the README and docs accurate and useful.
Use $write-tests to add tests that catch real bugs.
